title: DOT IIJA aggregate: obligation and outlay shares rise across a changing authority denominator
summary: From March 31, 2025 to May 31, 2026, reported DOT IIJA obligations rose from $272.869 billion to $392.472 billion and outlays from $143.257 billion to $237.220 billion; the obligated share moved from 67.30 to 71.92 percent and the outlay share from 35.33 to 43.47 percent. Denominator: Two DOT-wide formula-plus-discretionary IIJA financial statements; adjusted authority changed from $405.476 billion to $545.692 billion between observations.
key_findings: Finding: From March 31, 2025 to May 31, 2026, reported DOT IIJA obligations rose from $272.869 billion to $392.472 billion and outlays from $143.257 billion to $237.220 billion; the obligated share moved from 67.30 to 71.92 percent and the outlay share from 35.33 to 43.47 percent.
Denominator: Two DOT-wide formula-plus-discretionary IIJA financial statements; adjusted authority changed from $405.476 billion to $545.692 billion between observations.
Boundary: The denominator increased by about $140.216 billion, so percentage-point movement is not a fixed-cohort completion rate.
Boundary: Obligations and outlays are lifecycle measures, not accepted assets or outcomes.
Boundary: Two observations do not establish a durable trend or causal explanation.
